name: dimir frog

winrate_basis.why: The committed 2026-09-10 capture .protocol/raw-matchups.json holds a 'dimir control' row but no 'dimir frog' row, and this repository has validated no join between those two labels - the two 2026-09-10 captures are visibly different decks, one built on Psychic Frog and Tamiyo and the other on Snapcaster Mage and Wan Shi Tong. UNMEASURED rather than borrowed: reading the dimir control number onto this row would be an assertion the evidence does not support.

primary_gameplan: Cursed Totem is unusually good here and the reason is Psychic Frog: both 'Discard a card: Put a +1/+1 counter on this creature' and 'Exile three cards from your graveyard: This creature gains flying' are activated abilities of a creature, so a resolved Totem turns their best card into a 1/3 that cannot fly and cannot grow.
secondary_gameplan: Engineered Explosives at two counters destroys Psychic Frog, Tamiyo, Inquisitive Student and Orcish Bowmasters in one card; Cityscape Leveler's cast trigger gets value through their counterspells, and Walking Ballista picks off a Tamiyo before it flips.
opponent_gameplan: The ten committed 2026-09-10 lists are the tempo build: four Psychic Frog, four Thoughtseize, four Fatal Push, three Orcish Bowmasters, three Subtlety, three Force of Negation, two Tamiyo, Inquisitive Student and a Murktide Regent, on eighteen lands. The plan is to strip a card, counter the follow-up and win with a Frog that grows every time they discard a spare land. It interacts more cheaply than dimir control does and pressures faster.

opposing_sideboard_in.why: 10 of 10 committed 2026-09-10 lists; one blue mana counters a colorless spell or a cast trigger
9 of 10 committed lists; 'Nonbasic lands are Islands' shuts off twenty-one of our twenty-four lands
9 of 10 committed lists; the scaling answer to the cheap artifacts we fetch
8 of 10 committed lists; a life-paid sweeper that gets under Sire of Seven Deaths' ward

stance_rationale: Cursed Totem, Engineered Explosives, Cityscape Leveler and Walking Ballista are all one-sided here: we activate no creature abilities except Walking Ballista's own, and every fetch answers a card their deck cannot function without.

opponent_plan.posture_why: Thoughtseize and cheap permission come before the clock; the Frog only has to survive after the hand has already been taken apart.

key_cards.why: Named in the recorded gameplan; a two-mana threat that draws a card on damage and grows on every spare card discarded
Named in the recorded gameplan; four copies that take the Karn before it can fetch anything
Boarded body that turns our nonbasic manabase into Islands
Boarded counter aimed at our colorless spells and our cast triggers

play_plan.keep: A hand that still functions after one Thoughtseize and reaches four mana on its own.
play_plan.goldfish_for: Karn into Cursed Totem, which turns Psychic Frog into a 1/3 that cannot fly.
play_plan.watch_for: Two open mana on our turn three, which is Force of Negation or Spell Snare.
play_plan.posture_why: They trade one for one from an eighteen-land deck; Tron out-resources that if the Frog is answered.

survives_opposing_board.why: Engineered Explosives at two answers it, but a resolved Totem has already removed both of Psychic Frog's activated abilities, which is most of the card.
It sacrifices itself to its own ability, so their own Explosives cannot two-for-one it; two counters is reachable off Talisman of Resilience plus Giant's Boulder.
The destroy trigger is on cast, so Force of Negation and Consign to Memory still leave a permanent of theirs destroyed.
Fatal Push and Toxic Deluge answer it, but its counters can be removed for damage in response, so it kills a Tamiyo or an Orcish Bowmasters on the way out.

notes: Cursed Totem is not a hoser here, it is removal: Psychic Frog without its discard and its graveyard-exile abilities is a 1/3 ground creature with no evasion and no growth.

Consign to Memory counters triggered abilities as well as colorless spells, so a Devourer of Destiny cast into two open mana can lose its exile trigger and still resolve as a 5/5 - cast it when the trigger matters least.
Their Harbinger of the Seas is a creature, so Dismember and Walking Ballista both answer it; the maindeck Dismember should be saved for it once we have seen a board.
